explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model with high variance fits training noise, causing poor generalization on unseen validation data.

question: You notice a critical bug in production 30 minutes before end of day on Friday. The team lead is offline. What is your best course of action?
options: Assess the severity, notify the on-call engineer and post in the team incident channel with reproduction steps and a proposed hotfix.
Attempt to patch and deploy the fix directly to production immediately without code review.
Leave a note for Monday morning so the entire team can review it together during standup.
Ignore the issue assuming another senior engineer will notice it over the weekend.
rubricExplanations: 3 pts (Exemplary): Follows incident protocol, documents context, and alerts on-call without bypassing safety gates.
1 pt (Risky): Bypassing code review and deployment pipelines can cause severe cascading outages.
1 pt (Passive): Waiting until Monday leaves production broken for weekend users.
0 pts (Unacceptable): Neglecting production errors violates engineering ownership.
explanation: Best practice is transparent incident notification, documenting reproduction steps, and working with on-call engineers while upholding review safeguards.
